newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wages and salaries up 1.9 pct in Sept year.
newsitem.headline: NZ wages and salaries up 1.9 pct in Sept year.

text.p: New Zealand salaries and wage rates including overtime were up 1.9 percent in the September quarter against the September 1995 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
An increase of 0.6 percent in the latest quarter contributed to the annual rise.
Economists on average had expected an annual rise of 1.9 percent and 0.5 percent for the quarter.
Base salary and ordinary time wage rates in all sectors were on average 2.0 percent higher in the September quarter against the September 1995 quarter.
Overtime wage rates increased by 0.6 percent in the September quarter and rose by 1.3 percent over the September year, the same as for the years to June 1996 and September 1995.
Salary and wage rates paid in the public sector increased by 2.2 percent over the year, while rates in the private sector rose by 1.9 percent.
Central government rates rose 2.3 percent against local government rates of 1.9 percent.

SNZ said several setlements among government departments contributed to a 1.0 percent rise in the September quarter for the central government sector but other more recent central government settlements would be reflected in the December 1996 quarter.

The insurance and financing sector had the highest industry group increase in salary and wage rates over the year, up 2.6 percent. Next highest were machinery and metal products workers with 2.5 percent and central government services, up 2.4 percent.
The increase for the construction industry, at 1.7 percent, dipped below 2.0 percent for the first time in more than a year. The communication industry had the smallest increase of 0.6 percent.
Rises were recorded in all nine major occupation groups for the year with highest increases of 2.7 percent posted by professionals.

Friday's data comprises the wages and salaries component of the Labour Cost Index. Non-labour costs such as medical insurance and accident compensation premiums is released on December 13 when the full Labour Cost Index is released.
